research_notes: GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING for the 'does AKUT have a real under-18 track' question, but with an honest sourcing gap that drove NEEDS_REVIEW rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT. Confirmed FIRST on akut.org.tr directly (the search-and-rescue association, not AKUT Vakfı): core AKUT membership and 'Öğrenci Toplulukları' (Student Communities) are university-student-only ('university students and academics'); 'Genç AKUT' (akut.org.tr/genc-akut) is explicitly '9 – 12 Yaş Gurubu İlköğretim Öğrencileri' (ages 9-12, primary school); 'AKUT Junior' (akut.org.tr/akut-junior) is grades 5-8 (approx. ages 10-14), a school-club programme. All three confirmed too young/wrong-track for this batch's 14-18 lise target and NOT written up as separate records for that reason — a clean negative result. LABEP, run by the sister foundation AKUT Vakfı (akutvakfi.org.tr, not akut.org.tr), IS genuinely lise-targeted and IS currently active — but I could only confirm its CURRENT operation (2025-2026 school year, 20 weeks, Trabzon/TED Trabzon Koleji cohort) via independent local news (Taka Gazete, Kuzey Ekspres), not via a current, dedicated page on AKUT Vakfı's own site. The only AKUT Vakfı-hosted page I found describing LABEP in depth is dated to a 2013 workshop (4 schools: German School, Koç School, Austrian School, TED Eskişehir School). I could not find, on akutvakfi.org.tr, a current programme page stating how an individual student or unaffiliated school applies, what it costs, or a general (non-Trabzon-specific) age range. Local news does describe LABEP as implemented 'Türkiye genelinde' (nationwide) by AKUT, suggesting real recurrence beyond this one cohort. Net assessment: LABEP is real and appears to recur nationally, but a student/counselor relying only on the official AKUT Vakfı site right now would not find a clear, current, self-service application path — hence NEEDS_REVIEW, and cost/financial_aid left null rather than guessed at 0. CATEGORY JUDGMENT: classified volunteering_service for batch consistency with the other AKUT-family findings, though its content is more disaster-education/training than direct service delivery — a defensible alternative would be student_program; noted as ambiguous.

research_notes: AGE-RANGE CONFLICT recorded explicitly per instructions rather than silently resolved: Source A, Yeşilyurt Kent Konseyi's own Gençlik Meclisi Çalışma Yönergesi (fetched directly), states members are '15 – 30 yaş arasındaki kadın erkek eşitliğine dayanan [temsilciler]' — a range that includes this batch's 14-18 target band from age 15 up. Source B, a local news article (vanpostasigazetesi.com, secondary/non-official, NOT independently corroborated on an official page) covering a 2026 membership round for a body called 'Yeşilyurt Genç Meclis', states an explicit '18-30 yaş aralığında olmak' requirement with a 15-30 Aralık online-application window. These directly conflict. I could not fully resolve whether 'Yeşilyurt Genç Meclis' (described on the municipality's own yesilyurt.bel.tr site as launched in 2025 on the mayor's initiative) is the SAME body as the Kent Konseyi's statutory 'Gençlik Meclisi' governed by the 15-30 yönerge, under a shortened colloquial name, or a genuinely separate, newer municipal youth initiative running in parallel — yesilyurt.bel.tr's own article describes coordination between the two (the Kent Konseyi's General Secretary participated in the 2026 elections), suggesting overlap/close coordination rather than two unrelated bodies, but this does not settle the age-range question. PRACTICAL IMPLICATION: if 18-30 governs the currently-open enrollment round, a 15-17-year-old should NOT be told they can apply to the CURRENT cycle without checking directly first — the 15-30 figure comes from a standing bylaw that may not reflect this cycle's actual practice. I am deliberately not picking one number as 'the' answer. || LEGAL-BASIS LEAD (Belediye Kanunu 5393 madde 76 / kent konseyi yürütme kurulu ex-officio seat): I attempted to reach and directly read mevzuat.gov.tr's primary text of Belediye Kanunu No. 5393 Madde 76, as specifically requested, via 5 attempts: WebFetch of https://www.mevzuat.gov.tr/mevzuatmetin/1.5.5393.pdf (failed: 'unable to verify the first certificate', an SSL/TLS error), WebFetch of https://www.mevzuat.gov.tr/mevzuat?MevzuatNo=5393&MevzuatTur=1&MevzuatTertip=5 (failed: same certificate error), WebFetch of a Ministry of Industry .gov.tr mirror at sanayi.gov.tr/assets/pdf/birimler/SGMBelediyeKanunu.pdf (failed: fetch tool could not render/access the PDF), plus two targeted WebSearches for quoted article text. I DID NOT reach or directly read mevzuat.gov.tr, and — matching the discipline of the prior research lane that flagged this same lead — I am NOT citing Madde 76's specific text from memory or from a search engine's AI-generated summary as though I had read it myself. One WebSearch AI-overview (not a direct primary-source read, and not independently verified by me) characterised Madde 76 itself as a short article defining the Kent Konseyi's purpose (city vision, sustainable development, participation principles) without executive-board composition detail, attributing the specific 'executive board includes women's/youth council presidents' structural rule instead to the separate Kent Konseyi Yönetmeliği (a regulation issued under Madde 76's authority) — plausible (framework laws commonly delegate structural detail to an implementing yönetmelik) but explicitly flagged as an UNVERIFIED characterisation from a search summary, not a confirmed fact, since I could not open the law's or the regulation's own text myself. WHAT I COULD AND DID VERIFY DIRECTLY: the underlying structural fact itself — a youth/other council president holding an ex-officio ('doğal üye') seat on the kent konseyi's yürütme kurulu — on TWO different real municipalities' own official pages, fetched directly: this Yeşilyurt page states outright, of the Gençlik Meclisi başkanı specifically, 'Yeşilyurt Kent Konseyi Yürütme Kurulu'nun doğal üyesidir'; the Fethiye Gençlik Meclisi record in this same file quotes Fethiye Kent Konseyi's own page stating the equivalent rule generically for all meclis başkanları. Two independent municipal primary sources with near-identical language is reasonably strong evidence this is a nationally standardised rule (consistent with flowing from a national yönetmelik rather than each city coincidentally inventing the same wording), but I am explicitly NOT asserting the Madde 76 citation itself as confirmed, since I never read the primary statute text. NET: the underlying civic-structure fact is confirmed via direct primary municipal sources; the SPECIFIC LEGAL CITATION (5393 madde 76 itself, vs. the Kent Konseyi Yönetmeliği issued under it) could not be confirmed against mevzuat.gov.tr's own text despite genuine, repeated attempts — reported plainly as a limitation rather than guessed.

research_notes: PARTIAL VERIFICATION, included primarily as the third of the task's requested '2-3 municipal examples' and because it independently corroborates a structural finding. The page lists 'Gençlik Meclisi' as one of the kent konseyi's standing meclisler, and states generically for meclis başkanları (council presidents) as a class: 'Meclis Başkanı seçildiği andan itibaren, görev süresi olan 2 yıl boyunca Fethiye Kent Konseyi Yürütme Kurulunun doğal üyesi olur' (a council president becomes, from the moment of election, a natural/ex-officio member of the Fethiye Kent Konseyi Executive Board for their 2-year term). This is NOT phrased specifically about the gençlik meclisi başkanı, but as a general rule applying to all meclis başkanları, of which Gençlik Meclisi is one. This independently corroborates the same ex-officio pattern found explicitly named for the youth council specifically at Yeşilyurt (see that record for the full mevzuat.gov.tr primary-source attempt and its outcome). NOT FOUND for Fethiye specifically: a dedicated Gençlik Meclisi page giving its own age range, membership process, or current activity — I looked for one and did not find it in the time available, so age_range/selection_process are left null rather than assumed to mirror Yeşilyurt or Selçuklu. This record should be read as 'confirms the general Fethiye kent konseyi structure and the ex-officio pattern', not as 'a fully verified standalone Fethiye youth programme record' — hence NEEDS_REVIEW rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT.
